name: Tramadol
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: The selected US label is for extended-release tramadol, which should not be used in severe kidney impairment (creatinine clearance, CrCl, below 30 mL/min) because its fixed strengths do not allow safe dose adjustment. Tramadol and its active metabolite (M1) build up as kidney function falls.

bands.recommendation: ER: no consistent change in tramadol exposure at CrCl 30–80; M1 exposure 20–40% higher (label). Use with caution.
bands.short: ER: no change; use with caution

bands.recommendation: ER: do not use (label). Immediate-release (IR) tramadol: not covered by the selected label; specialist input.
bands.short: ER: do not use; IR: specialist

bands.recommendation: ER: do not use (label). IR: not covered; specialist input.
bands.short: ER: do not use; IR: specialist

hd.text: ER: do not use (severe impairment). Less than 7% of tramadol and M1 removed in 4 hours of dialysis (label).

pd.text: ER: do not use. No PD data.

crrt.text: ER: do not use. No data.

dialyzable: No: less than 7% removed in a 4-hour dialysis (label).
monitoring: Respiratory depression, sedation, seizures, serotonin syndrome, hypoglycemia, hyponatremia; opioid boxed warnings.

pediatric.approved_ages: Not established in pediatric patients. Contraindicated under 12 years, and under 18 years after tonsillectomy and/or adenoidectomy (label).

renal.recommendation: Not established in children; contraindicated under 12 years.

pediatric.notes: Avoid in adolescents 12 to 18 years with risk factors for respiratory depression (obstructive sleep apnea, obesity, severe lung or neuromuscular disease) (label).

adult: IMPORTANT: Fetcher chose an extended-release capsule label (Trigen, NDA022370). Most PH tramadol products are immediate-release (often with paracetamol). The IR (Ultram) label has CrCl <30 interval-extension dosing; it was NOT available, so IR rows say 'specialist input'. Fetch the IR label before approval.
Label text contains an apparent error: 'severe renal impairment (Child-Pugh Class C)'. Child-Pugh is a liver score. Do not reproduce.
pediatric: Contraindicated under 12 years per label; nothing extrapolated.
